Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Kabc020037762022 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.712/2022 Dated this 8th day of October, 2025 Petitioner: Sumanth R. Gowda S/o Ramaiah, Aged about 21 years, Residing at No.1, 3rd Cross, 17th Main Road, Ragavanagar, Muneshwara Block, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru, Karnataka - 560 026. ( Sri N. Shivaram, Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. Bheema S/o Sabanna Bhimashappanor, Aged about major, Residing at No.1/45, near Masjid, Ganapur, Yadgir District, Karnataka - 585 321. 2 MVC No.712/2022 Also residing at No.224, 10th Cross, Rajanna Colony, near Church, Nagawarapalya, Bengaluru, Karnataka - 560 093. (RC owner of the TATA ACE Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/ 1 bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294) (Sri K.V. Pradeepa, Advocate) 2. Fayaz Ahamed, Age: Major, Residing at 146/1, 1st Block, Kambipura, Kumbalagodu, Bengaluru, Karnataka - 560 060. (Insurance holder of the TATA ACE bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294) (Ex-parte) 3.
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 09-12-2021 at about 7.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as cleaner in Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-41-C- 5886, driven by its driver from Bengaluru to Tumkur, carefully, by following all the traffic rules. When the petitioner reached Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 highway road, near Sharapura Palya Gate, Nelamangala Taluk, at that time the driver of the Tata Ace bearing No.KA-53-C-5294 came from same direction, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without following the traffic rules and suddenly drove the same from the right side to left side. Due to which, the Canter in which the petitioner was traveling dashed to Tata Ace vehicle. Due to the said impact, the Canter fell on the road and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Harsha M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/ 2 took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, he was working as cleaner and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said TATA ACE, for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 3 have appeared through their counsel. The respondent No.3 has filed its written statement. The respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has denied involvement of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C- 5294 in the alleged accident and the manner in which the accident has taken place.
texts.arguments: It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the present petition. Further it is contended that, the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C- 5886 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, on the date of the accident. Further it is contended that, the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 was not at all responsible for the cause of accident, as the driver of the said Tata Ace was moving slowly, cautiously and on the correct side of the road. As such this respondent is not a necessary and proper party for the adjudication of the above petition. Further it is contended that, the driver of the canter bearing Reg. No.KA- 41-C-5886 drove the same, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without maintaining safety distance in between the vehicles and in the process of overtaking the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the rear portion of the moving Tata Ace vehicle and thereby caused the accident. Further it is contended that, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the rear portion of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C- 5294 is damaged and front portion of the canter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-5886 is damaged. Hence, it is clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the canter. The said sequence of events clearly establishes that, the driver of the Tata Ace has been wrongly/intentionally implicated by the Police in the charge-sheet as accused No.1 and the obvious intention is to fasten the liability against the respondent insurance company by taking advantage of the policy of insurance. Hence, there cannot be any liability against this respondent insurance company as driver of the Tata Ace vehicle was not at all responsible for the cause of the accident. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 in favour of respondent No.2 and it was valid for the period from 06-12- 2021 to 05-12-2022. Further it is contended that, the owner of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 has willfully entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not had a valid and Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/ 3 effective driving licence to drive the same on the date of the accident and as such the respondent No.2 is guilty of breach of the terms and conditions of the policy and as a result of the same this respondent is not liable to indemnify the insured and accordingly the above petition is liable to be dismissed against it. It has seek protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.3, to show that, the above Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/ 6 medical records are false documents. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 22 years is 18. The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
